name: Fedora
summary: A community-driven Linux distribution sponsored by Red Hat, focused on modern technologies, security, and upstream development.

content.introduction: Fedora is a general-purpose Linux distribution developed by the Fedora Project and sponsored by Red Hat. It is known for adopting modern Linux technologies relatively early while maintaining a strong focus on open-source software and security.
content.what_is_it: Fedora provides a complete operating system built around the Linux kernel. Rather than being designed for a single specialized purpose, it offers editions and variants covering desktop computing, servers, development, containers, and other use cases.
content.how_it_works: A Fedora system combines the Linux kernel with a collection of system components, libraries, services, applications, and development tools. Its traditional package ecosystem is based on RPM packages and is primarily managed through DNF.

privacy.overview: Fedora provides a relatively strong foundation for users who want a transparent and open-source operating system. However, using Fedora does not automatically make a system private. Privacy depends on the applications, online services, telemetry, browser configuration, and user practices built on top of the operating system.
weaknesses: Some default services may communicate with external servers
Privacy depends heavily on the applications and services chosen by the user

security.overview: Security is one of Fedora's major strengths. The distribution integrates technologies such as SELinux and secure boot support while benefiting from rapid security updates.

content.usability: Fedora is relatively accessible to Linux newcomers while still providing the flexibility expected by experienced Linux users. Its default GNOME desktop provides a polished environment, while other desktop environments are available through official variants.
content.performance: Performance depends heavily on the chosen desktop environment, hardware, applications, and configuration. Fedora itself is not specifically designed to be an ultra-lightweight distribution, although lighter desktop environments can be used.
who_is_it_for: Users looking for a modern Linux desktop
Users interested in recent Linux technologies
Users who value open-source software and security
who_is_it_not_for: Users requiring extremely long-term software stability
Users looking for the absolute lightest possible Linux system
Users who depend heavily on proprietary software unavailable on Linux
disadvantages: Updates can be more frequent than on conservative distributions
Some proprietary software requires additional configuration
content.verdict: Fedora is a strong general-purpose Linux distribution for users who want a modern, secure, and open-source computing environment without having to build their system from scratch.
